paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Pharaoh was thrashing around like a monster in his own rivers, muddying the streams with his feet. Then the Lord GOD says, "I will spread My net over you…" (Ezekiel 32:3). No power is too big to be answerable to God, and I do NOT care how loud it splashes.

Now look at what stays still when the splashing stops. God says, "Then I will let her waters settle…" (Ezekiel 32:14). I think that's the quiet kind of ending nobody expected, because the mud was never going to clear itself. If your life feels stirred up by somebody else's pride, remember who is in charge of the waters.

And here's why it matters to you. God says it all happens so "they will know that I am the LORD" (Ezekiel 32:15). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer sure nobody was running anything, and I was wrong, friend. Trust the One who holds the net, keep your oven ready, and let Him be the One who is God.
